copilot-pull-request-reviewer re-reviewed the round-4 fix commit and raised 2 NEW in-scope findings on the sweep-eval/aggregate path (same regression class as the original threads: Floor-2 misclassification + a fan-in trust-boundary hole). Both FIXED (rule #12). (1) deriveRunFacts applies Floor-1 safe-room active-time credit unconditionally, but sweep-eval accepts --floor and would score a Floor-2 batch with Floor-1 win semantics. The tool is Floor-1-calibrated by construction (budgetMs is always FLOOR1_TIME_BUDGET_MS; no Floor-2 budget exists), so threading floorId into deriveRunFacts would be uncalibrated. Instead enforce the Floor-1 precondition at BOTH boundaries: sweep-eval parseArgs now throws on --floor != floor1; ShardMeta gains a floorId field (written by buildMeta); mergeShards rejects a non-floor1 first-shard meta AND a cross-shard floorId mismatch; deriveRunFacts docstring documents the precondition. (2) the schema-version guard proves safeRoomMs is EXPECTED at v2 but not that a row HAS a sane value — an omitted field (activeTimeMs ?? 0) silently restores raw-time classification, a value > gameTimeMs clamps active time to 0 (manufacturing an official win for any victory), and NaN misclassifies as a loss. Added assertRowSafeRoomInRange validating finite gameTimeMs>=0 and finite safeRoomMs in [0, gameTimeMs], called at the mergeShards row-loop fan-in boundary. Tests: all-floor2-batch rejection + a safeRoomMs domain it.each (missing/NaN/negative/over-gameTimeMs). verify:fast green; aggregate-shards unit test 36/36.

copilot-pull-request-reviewer re-reviewed the round-5 fix commit (c8372d08) and raised 1 finding on scoring.ts:122: the strict `<` budget comparison could misclassify an exact-budget run because gameTimeMs is ACCUMULATED (repeated += GAME.DELTA_MS, simulation-step.ts:120) while safeRoomMs is a MULTIPLICATION (safeRoomFrames * GAME.DELTA_MS, headless-runner.ts), so activeTimeMs = gameTimeMs - safeRoomMs carries FP drift; the reviewer claimed the 21_600-frame boundary could represent slightly BELOW 360_000 and count an exact-budget run as a win, and asked to cover the case with a value accumulated from GAME.DELTA_MS. INVESTIGATED (numerical experiment in Node, faithful to the real runner which always steps GAME.DELTA_MS): 1000/60 = 16.666666666666668 rounds UP in IEEE-754, so repeated addition drifts UPWARD -> accumulate(21_600) = 360000.00000005 (ABOVE budget) -> `< 360000` = false = correctly a loss (matches the game's `elapsed >= deadline` timeout). Every mixed accumulate-minus-multiply case with 21_600 active frames also landed active > 360_000 -> correctly a loss; 21_599 frames = 359983.33 -> a win. The drift magnitude (~5e-8 ms) is ~8 orders of magnitude below the 16.67 ms frame quantum, so it can NEVER flip an adjacent-frame classification, and 360_000/(1000/60) = 21_600 is an EXACT integer so the budget maps to a real boundary frame. The reviewer's suggested `< budget + epsilon` tolerance would INTRODUCE a bug (flip the exact-budget run to a win, contradicting the timeout semantics). ADJUDICATION (rule #12 - fix the test/gate around the requirement, never the requirement around a review): production code is provably correct -> NO scoring.ts change; instead LOCKED the boundary with a test-only regression suite in scoring-official-win.test.ts that mirrors the runner's accumulation + multiplication forms and asserts exact-budget = loss / one-frame-under = win / accumulate-minus-multiply boundary correct (commit 439755fe). Directly answers the reviewer's 'cover the case using a value accumulated from GAME.DELTA_MS' ask and protects the boundary against a future DELTA_MS change. verify:fast green; scoring-official-win 16/16.
